title: Casebook Ivory — Bluebook Holding Statement
description: A law-journal slide structured around a Bluebook citation header and bold-serif holding statement, with numbered argument paragraphs, superscript footnote markers, and a hairline-ruled footnote block that mirrors the typographic discipline of a printed Harvard Law Review page.
philosophy: This template treats the slide as a printed page, not a screen object — it borrows its entire visual grammar from American law-review typography: Bluebook citation strings, indented numbered paragraphs, and a hairline rule separating argument from authority. It refuses decorative imagery, colour washes, and bullet-point compression, because legal argument lives in structured prose, not fragments. The oxblood holding statement is the sole chromatic gesture, signalling where doctrine is declared without editorialising further. Built for speakers who need their slides to withstand the same scrutiny as the brief itself.
goodFor: Moot court and appellate argument overviews
Legal-brief companion slides with full Bluebook citation strings
Academic conference panels dissecting specific court holdings
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business or financial reviews
Consumer-facing product or brand pitch decks
Audiences unfamiliar with Bluebook or law-review citation conventions
Fast-paced decks requiring visual variety and mixed layout types across slides
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like the masthead page of a bound law review volume — austere, unapologetically text-driven, and commanding through restraint rather than decoration. Compositional drama emerges entirely from the contrast between the small, precise citation string at the crown and the weighty holding-statement title that dominates the center, with the oxblood accent on that declaration functioning as the sole chromatic gesture. The mood is scholarly authority: cool ivory ground, two hairline rules imposing vertical discipline, and nothing competing with the primacy of the legal argument. Avoid any photographic element, illustrative mark, tonal wash, or asymmetric composition that would betray the printed-page grammar.

examples.layoutNotes: Single centered content column spanning roughly 60% of slide width, flanked by symmetrical outer margins that echo a law-review page trim. Vertical layout divides into three bands: a top citation strip holding a Bluebook-style reference string, separated from the body by a hairline rule; a dominant title zone occupying the central third of the slide; and a bottom author-attribution strip anchored by a second hairline rule above it. No imagery zone or header band; a folio mark or institution identifier may sit outside the content column at bottom-right.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads as a single typeset page lifted from a printed law review — austere, deliberate, and undecorated, with no imagery, tint washes, or spatial looseness to soften its authority. The holding statement commands attention through weight contrast alone, its oxblood tint the single chromatic gesture in an otherwise ink-on-ivory field. Numbered paragraphs carry the sequential, self-contained rhythm of a filed brief — never compressed into fragments or bullets. The hairline-ruled footnote band at the foot grounds every assertion in cited authority, reinforcing the expectation that each claim on this slide could withstand appellate scrutiny.

examples.layoutNotes: Single-column text well sits in cols 2–11 of a 12-col grid with an 8% outer margin, preserving the impression of a printed page rather than a projected screen. The top zone holds a Bluebook citation string flush-left as a document header, immediately followed by a bold-serif holding statement in oxblood that spans the full text well as the primary hierarchy anchor. Below it, two to three numbered argument paragraphs are indented uniformly, separated by tight leading rather than visual gutters, sustaining dense prose rhythm. A hairline rule drawn at roughly 72% of page height divides the argument body from a compact footnote band of two to three lines, with superscript reference markers echoed from their inline callouts above.
